content.title: About
content.content: Cooked lotus root (Nelumbo nucifera) is the edible rhizome of the lotus plant. After cooking it retains a crisp texture and a mildly sweet, nutty flavor. In Asian cuisines it is used in soups, salads, stir‑fries, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lotus root has a distinctive pattern of holes that looks like a star when sliced.
In Chinese and Japanese cooking it is often sliced thin and quickly stir‑fried.
The lotus is a symbol of purity and rebirth in Buddhism and Taoism.
Raw lotus root can be slightly bitter; cooking removes the bitterness.
Traditional Chinese medicine uses lotus root to aid digestion and strengthen the lungs.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion, helps maintain satiety, and regulates blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and provides antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked lotus root is low in calories, making it a good choice for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lotus, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Water‑borne contamination
items.content: Lotus grows in stagnant water, so thorough washing and proper cooking are essential to avoid microbial contamination.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High oxalate levels may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked lotus root can be sliced thin and added to salads, soups, stews, or stir‑fries. It is also used in sushi rolls and as a rice side dish. Before cooking, peel the outer skin and rinse well.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked lotus root in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Fresh roots keep best in a cool, humid environment and should be used within a week.
